rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After forbidding alliance with disbelievers, God commands allegiance to those who deserve it.
rows.anchor: لما نهى في الآيات المتقدمة عن موالاة الكفار أمر في هذه الآية بموالاة من يجب موالاته

rows.speaker: عبادة بن الصامت
rows.claim: After ʿUbādah renounced his pact with Qurayẓa and Naḍīr and declared allegiance to God and His Messenger, the verse was revealed in accord with him.
rows.anchor: عبادة بن الصامت لما تبرأ من اليهود

rows.speaker: عبدالله بن سلام
rows.claim: Ibn Salām said his people ostracized him and distance prevented him from joining the Prophet’s companions; the verse came, and they accepted God, the Messenger, and believers as allies.
rows.anchor: وروي أيضا أن عبدالله بن سلام قال : يا رسول الله إن قومنا قد هجرونا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the general reading, every believer is an ally of every other believer, as 9:71 also states.
rows.anchor: فعلى هذا : الآية عامة في حق كل المؤمنين ، فكل من كان مؤمنا فهو ولي كل المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prayer and almsgiving description distinguishes sincere believers from hypocrites who claim faith but neglect prayer and are miserly; the cited descriptions are 9:54, 4:142, and 33:19.
rows.anchor: والمراد بذكر هذه الصفلات تمييز عن المنافقين

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abū Muslim takes rukūʿ as submission: they pray and give alms while obedient and humble toward all God’s commands and prohibitions.
rows.anchor: قال أبو مسلم : المراد من الركوع الخضوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view reads rukūʿ as prayer bowing, singled out to honor it, as in the command to bow with those who bow (2:43).
rows.anchor: وخص الركوع بالذكر تشريفا له كما في قوله { واركعوا مع الراكعين }

words: ٱلَّذِينَ يُقِيمُونَ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَيُؤْتُونَ ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ وَهُمْ رَٰكِعُونَ
rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say the companions were at different stages when it was revealed: some had finished prayer, some gave to a poor person, and some were still bowing, so all states are mentioned.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم : إن أصحابه كانوا عند نزول هذه الآية مختلفون

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: ʿIkrimah reports that the verse was revealed concerning Abū Bakr.
rows.anchor: روى عكرمة أن هذه الآية نزلت في أبي بكر رضي الله عنه

rows.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: ʿAṭāʾ reports from Ibn ʿAbbās that the verse was revealed concerning ʿAlī.
rows.anchor: روى عطاء عن ابن عباس أنها نزلت في علي بن أبي طالب عليه السلام

rows.speaker: عبدالله بن سلام
rows.claim: Ibn Salām says he saw ʿAlī give his ring to a needy person while bowing, and concluded that they should ally with him.
rows.anchor: روي أن عبدالله بن سلام قال : لما نزلت هذه الآية قلت يا رسول أنا رأيت عليا تصدق بخاتمه

rows.speaker: أبو ذر
rows.claim: Abū Dharr recounts a petitioner receiving no alms, then ʿAlī signaling him to take his ring while bowing; the Prophet prayed for ʿAlī as his minister, and Gabriel brought the verse. No grading is given.
rows.anchor: وروي عن أبي ذر رضي الله عنه أنه قال : صليت مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يوما صلاة الظهر ، فسأل سائل

rows.speaker: الشيعة
rows.claim: The Shīʿa argue that the verse proves ʿAlī is the imam after the Prophet, reasoning that it identifies an imam and then identifying him as ʿAlī.
rows.anchor: قالت الشيعة : هذه الآية دالة على أن الإمام بعد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم هو علي بن أبي طالب

rows.speaker: الشيعة
rows.claim: They argue that wali can mean both helper or beloved and one with authority; since the meanings can coexist, the righteous believers named here govern the community. They cite the guardian in a marriage report as usage evidence.
rows.anchor: قالت الشيعة : هذه الآية دالة على أن الإمام بعد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم هو علي بن أبي طالب

rows.speaker: الشيعة
rows.claim: Their second argument says innamā excludes a general meaning of support, leaving authority as the only other sense of wali; thus the described believers have authority over the whole community.
rows.anchor: قالت الشيعة : هذه الآية دالة على أن الإمام بعد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم هو علي بن أبي طالب

rows.speaker: القوم
rows.claim: They infer ʿAlī specifically: all who take the verse to establish a particular imam identify him as ʿAlī; they reject Abū Bakr because that would imply his imamate, which they say the community does not accept from this verse.
rows.anchor: وهذا حاصل استدلال القوم بهذه الآية على إمامة علي عليه السلام

rows.speaker: القوم
rows.claim: They say the bowing clause cannot coordinate with the prior description because prayer already includes bowing; it must be circumstantial, making giving alms while bowing specific to ʿAlī and proving his imamate.
rows.anchor: وهذا حاصل استدلال القوم بهذه الآية على إمامة علي عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī rejects combining wali’s shared meanings of helper and authority: legal theory does not allow a homonym to bear both meanings at once.
rows.anchor: أما حمل لفظ الولي على الناصر وعلى المتصرف معا فغير جائز ، لما ثبت في أصول الفقه أنه لا يجوز حمل اللفظ المشترك على مفهومية معا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surrounding bans on taking Jews and Christians as allies in 5:51 and 5:57 show that wali here means helper and beloved; an imamate reading would interrupt a continuous argument.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن الولاية المأمور بها ههنا هي المنهي عنها فيما قبل ، ولما كانت الولاية المنهي عنها فيما قبل هي الولاية بمعنى النصرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Authority over the community did not belong to ʿAlī during the Prophet’s life, whereas love and support already did; the paired prohibition and command must apply at the same time.
rows.anchor: لأن علي بن أبي طالب كرم الله وجهه ما كان نافذ التصرف حال حياة الرسول ، والآية تقتضي كون هؤلاء المؤمنون موصوفين بالولاية في الحال

words: وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ ٱلَّذِينَ يُقِيمُونَ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَيُؤْتُونَ ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ وَهُمْ رَٰكِعُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The description uses plural forms repeatedly in seven places; applying them to one person is possible only figuratively, while the literal reading is a group.
rows.anchor: أنه تعالى ذكر المؤمنين الموصوفين في هذه الآية بصيغة الجمع في سبعة مواضع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī says 5:54 strongly supports Abū Bakr’s imamate; reading 5:55 as ʿAlī’s immediate imamate would make the verses contradictory, so it cannot prove that succession.
rows.anchor: من أقوى الدلائل على صحة إمامة أبي بكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAlī knew Qurʾānic interpretation yet, when arguing at the council, cited the Ghadīr report, mutual invocation, and his merits but never this verse; Rāzī treats that silence as defeating the Shīʿī proof.
rows.anchor: وليس للقوم أن يقولوا : إنه تركه للتقية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if the verse implies ʿAlī’s imamate, it gives no date; Rāzī accepts an imamate after Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, and ʿUthmān, since ʿAlī lacked authority during the Prophet’s life.
rows.anchor: بعد أبي بكر وعمر وعثمان ، إذ ليس في الآية ما يدل على تعيين الوقت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī rejects the claim that only two community positions are possible: the non-immediate reading is a third possibility, and the objection could naturally arise alongside the original proof.
rows.anchor: من الظاهر أنه منذ استدل مستدل بهذه الآية على إمامة علي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The community already knew God and His Messenger had authority; the verse reassures them that divine support leaves no need for alliance with unbelievers, so wali means supporter and beloved, not both homonymous senses.
rows.anchor: وإنما ذكر الله تعالى هذا الكلام تطييبا لقول المؤمنين وتعريفا لهم بأنه لا حاجة بهم إلى اتخاذ الأحباب والأنصار من الكفار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because wali occurs once, Rāzī says it cannot mean support and authority simultaneously under the rule against combining a homonym’s meanings.
rows.anchor: ولا شك أن لفظ الولي مذكور مرة واحدة ، فلما أريد به ههنا معنى النصرة امتنع أن يراد به معنى التصرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reading wali as love and support matches 5:54: its love and support descriptions are reaffirmed here, while its striving description parallels prayer and almsgiving in 5:55.
rows.anchor: على معنى المحبة والنصرة كان قوله { إنما وليكم الله ورسوله } يفيد فائدة قوله { يحبهم ويحبونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī denies that innamā always restricts meaning, citing 10:24 and 47:36, where worldly life is called a likeness or play and diversion without excluding other descriptions.
rows.anchor: ولا نسلم أن كلمة { إنما } للحصر ، والدليل عليه قوله { إنما مثل الحيواة الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse can address one group as those under protection and name another as allies; support by the latter for the former need not be universal or self-support.
rows.anchor: أنه تعالى قسم المؤمنين قسمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thus restricting the specified allies does not rule out support as the meaning of wali; Rāzī calls this a subtle answer requiring reflection.
rows.anchor: فثبت أن نصرة أحد قسمي الأمة غير ثابتة لكل الأمة ، بل مخصوصة بالقسم الثاني من الأمة ، فلم يلزم من كون الولاية المذكورة في هذه الآية خاصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī denies that the verse is specifically about ʿAlī: most commentators apply it to the whole community and its instruction to take Muslim allies; some say it concerns Abū Bakr.
rows.anchor: فقد بينا أن أكثر المفسرين زعموا أنه في حق الأمة ، والمراد أن الله تعالى أمر المسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zakah ordinarily means obligatory alms (2:43); paying it late while bowing would delay a duty beyond its first time, sinful according to most scholars, so Rāzī rejects this attribution to ʿAlī and a voluntary-charity reading.
rows.anchor: أن الزكاة اسم للواجب لا للمندوب بدليل قوله تعالى { وإذ أخذنا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī argues that ʿAlī should be absorbed in remembering God during prayer and unable to attend to another’s speech, invoking 3:191.
rows.anchor: أن اللائق بعلي عليه السلام أن يكون مستغرق القلب بذكر الله حال ما يكون في الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī says ʿAlī had no wealth subject to obligatory zakah: the Shīʿī account that three loaves brought the praise of Sūrat al-Insān (76:1) implies poverty, so the ring gift cannot be the zakah meant here.
rows.anchor: فإنهم يقولون : إنه لما أعطى ثلاثة أقراص نزل فيه سورة { أهل * أتى }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even granting that the verse refers to ʿAlī, the argument proves imamate only if wali means authority rather than support or love, which Rāzī has already rejected.
rows.anchor: هب أن المراد بهذه الآية هو علي بن أبي طالب لكنه لم يتم الاستدلال بالآية إلا إذا تم أن المراد بالولي هو المتصرف لا الناصر والمحب

rows.speaker: القائلون
rows.claim: Those who take the verse to mean giving alms while bowing infer that a small action, such as handing charity to a petitioner during prayer, does not invalidate prayer.
rows.anchor: الذين يقولون : المراد من قوله { ويؤتون الزكواة وهم راكعون } هو أنهم يؤتون الزكاة حال كونهم راكعين احتجوا بالآية على أن العمل القليل لا يقطع الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular wali makes God the primary source of allegiance, with the Messenger and believers included derivatively; a plural ‘allies’ would lose this primary-and-subordinate structure.
rows.anchor: أصل الكلام إنما وليكم الله ، فجعلت الولاية لله على طريق الأصالة ، ثم نظم في سلك إثباتها له إثباتها لرسول الله والمؤمنين على سبيل التبع

rows.speaker: عبد الله
rows.claim: A reading attributed to ʿAbd Allāh has mawlākum, ‘your protector/master,’ in place of waliyyukum.
rows.anchor: وفي قراءة عبد الله : إنما مولاكم الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase is parsed as nominative apposition to the preceding ‘those’ (as transmitted in the text), or as the predicate ‘they are those who pray,’ or as accusative for praise.
rows.anchor: الجواب : الرفع على البدل من { الذين كفروا } أو يقال : هم الذين يقيمون ، أو النصب على المدح

words: ٱلَّذِينَ يُقِيمُونَ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَيُؤْتُونَ ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ وَهُمْ رَٰكِعُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The description distinguishes sincere believers from hypocritical claimants: sincere devotion is known through regular prayer, including bowing understood as humility and submission to God.
rows.anchor: والغرض من ذكره تمييز المؤمن المخلص عمن يدعي الإيمان ويكون منافقا ، لأن ذلك الإخلاص إنما يعرف بكونه مواظبا على الصلاة في حال الركوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening is best read as continuing the angels’ rebuke in 6:93, with the whole speech reported by angels charged either with taking souls or with punishment.
rows.anchor: أن يكون هذا معطوفا على قول الملائكة { أخرجوا أنفسكم اليوم تجزون عذاب الهون بما كنتم تقولون } فبين تعالى أنهم كما يقولون ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative makes God the speaker; the issue is whether He speaks to disbelievers, since ‘He will not speak to them’ seems to deny it while 15:92 and 7:6 describe questioning. Rāzī prefers the angel-speech reading because of the conjunction.
rows.anchor: والقول الثاني : أن قائل هذا القول هو الله تعالى ومنشأ هذا الاختلاف إن الله تعالى هل يتكلم مع الكفار أو لا ؟

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: Ibn Qutaybah treats furādā as the plural of fardān, like sukkārā from sukkārān and kusālā from kaslān.
rows.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة : فرادى جمع فردان ، مثل سكارى وسكران

rows.speaker: غيره
rows.claim: Another grammarian takes furādā as plural of farīd, by analogy with ridāfā and radīf.
rows.anchor: وقال غيره فرادى : جمع فريد ، مثل ردافى ورديف

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ lists four possible singular forms: fard, farda, farīd, and fardān.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء : فرادى جمع واحده فرد وفردة وفريد وفردان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rebuke recalls that people spent their effort gaining wealth and status and worshipping idols as intercessors; at resurrection the wealth is gone and idols cannot intercede, leaving them alone.
rows.anchor: المراد منه التقريع والتوبيخ ، وذلك لأنهم صرفوا جدهم وجهدهم في الدنيا إلى تحصيل أمرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers spent life gaining true knowledge and righteous deeds; these remain with them in their graves and at resurrection, so they arrive with provisions for the afterlife rather than truly alone.
rows.anchor: بخلاف أهل الإيمان فإنهم صرفوا عمرهم إلى تحصيل المعارف الحقة

rows.speaker: نافع وحفص عن عاصم والكسائي
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ, Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim, and al-Kisāʾī read baynakum in the accusative; it denotes the partnership or association that had joined them.
rows.anchor: قرأ نافع وحفص عن عاصم والكسائي { بينكم } بالنصب

rows.speaker: الباقون
rows.claim: The remaining readers use the nominative, construing bayn as the bond or connection that has been severed.
rows.anchor: والباقون بالرفع قال الزجاج : الرفع أجود ، ومعناه ، لقد تقطع وصلكم

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj prefers the nominative reading, ‘your bond has been severed’; he accepts the accusative as meaning that the association between them has been severed.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج : الرفع أجود ، ومعناه ، لقد تقطع وصلكم

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abū ʿAlī distinguishes a declinable noun like ‘separation’ from the preferable adverbial form, which can be reused as a noun; the cited usage in 41:5 and 18:78 supports this, while a maṣdar reading would distort the intended sense.
rows.anchor: قال أبو علي : هذا الاسم يستعمل على ضربين : أحدهما : أن يكون اسما منصرفا كالافتراق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the root suggests separation, bayn can denote a bond because it is used of two parties joined in some respect, such as partnership or kinship.
rows.anchor: هذا اللفظ إنما يستعمل في الشيئين اللذين بينهما مشاركة ومواصلة من بعض الوجوه ، كقولهم بيني وبينه شركة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For the accusative reading, the subject is understood: ‘your bond has been severed among you.’
rows.anchor: أما من قرأ { لقد تقطع بينكم } بالنصب فوجهه أنه أضمر الفاعل والتقدير : لقد تقطع وصلكم بينكم

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sībawayh compares the ellipsis to ‘when it is tomorrow, come to me,’ where hope or misfortune is understood from context.
rows.anchor: وقال سيبويه : إنهم قالوا إذا كان غدا فأتني والتقدير : إذا كان الرجاء أو البلاء غدا فأتني

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī supplies the omitted subject as mā baynakum, ‘what was between you,’ omitted because its meaning is clear.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن الأنباري : التقدير : لقد تقطع ما بينكم
